chapter: Growing up: theaters and the lakefront
title: Learning theater music by heart; Augie Shelang; hotel ballrooms
summary: Hirsch explains that hearing the Liberty's music daily let him play it at the Sanger without reading well; he also recalls Augie Shelang and dance rooms at the Jung and Roosevelt hotels.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Yeah, well Louie was down there, well I got to know Louie from when I was playing with dance orchestras and things like that before I got into the theater. In fact, I used to...this is funny. There was a fellow by the name of Augie Shelang. You've heard of him.
I've seen him but I never... He was nuts.

He was absolutely out of his mind. He was a drummer. He was a good rhythm drummer. Couldn't read note as big as a house. He was working down on Bourbon and Bienville Street. And I went down there one night. I felt like playing jazz. I was playing at the theater. Oh, I forgot to tell you this. Having worked at the Liberty Theater as an usher and hearing the music, hearing that music every day, every day, every day, three times, four times a day, I got to know it by heart. And when I went to the Sanger Theater, they used that same music from the Liberty because it's all Sanger Amusement Company. They used the same music for the newsweekly. In other words, we used to...they used to cut the sound on a newsweekly for the title and then open the sound for voice when the picture came on. And we had all of that music that they were playing over at the Liberty Theater. This is what we were playing at the Sanger. And the guy said, man, you sure know how to read good.
I didn't know how to read. I remember the guy that memorized it.

So, I didn't know how to read, but I mean...I didn't have to read. I knew the damn stuff I thought. But it was funny. It's a funny situation. It was really something else. So I was a kid. I was only 24 years old. I was a kid.
That's when you went into the Sanger Tour. Yeah.

I was at the Jung Hotel with Alice Stratikas. That used to be a beautiful place, the roof garden. I think they used to charge you 50 cents or a dollar for a drink or something like that. Dance all night for a dollar and a half or two dollars. Beautiful room. They used to have a ceiling in it that used to slide over and you could see the sky right from the top. They don't have it anymore up there, I don't think.

And then we also had on the 13th floor of the Roosevelt Hotel, they had a big room up there. There was a ball, like a ballroom. They've cut that up and made storage places and made that imperial bedroom up there for dignitaries. Made a whole suite up there. But this is...
